beats.narration_text: Hello, I am Muskan Agrawal, and this video is a summary of Week Two of the Humanitarians AI website restructure: typography refinement, hero concepting, and a link level audit of the navigation and footer. Week One produced opinions. Week Two turned them into numbers.

Week One ended with a decision: no full rebuild. Fix the structural problems first, reassess later. Week Two is the first half of that promise, and it starts by making the problems specific enough to argue with.
A phased plan needs a priority order. A priority order needs measurements. So every claim in this video was measured against the live site, not estimated by eye.

Start with navigation. The primary bar carries seven destinations: the logo, four section links, and two buttons. About Us and Contact Us are not among them. For a nonprofit, those are the two links a first time visitor hunts for, and they live only in the hero and the footer.
beats.new_visual_element: Hero screenshot, red boxes on the four section links and the two CTA buttons

shot.hold_reason: annotation boxes measured from 01_hero_section.jpg pixels — see SHOTLIST.md

beats.narration_text: Mapped out, the bar reads as four content sections and two calls to action competing for the same strip. One label, A I plus one, tells a stranger nothing about what sits behind it. Orientation links are missing; promotion links are duplicated.
beats.new_visual_element: Drawn nav map — 7 slots across, 2 absent orientation slots below

beats.narration_text: Then the footer, audited at the link level. Six columns, thirty three links inside them, thirty nine anchors in total. That is a fine place for depth, and a poor place to be carrying orientation.
beats.new_visual_element: Footer screenshot, red box on the Projects column, running count chips

beats.narration_text: The Projects column is the largest, at eleven links. Six of them are bare proper nouns a first time visitor cannot decode: Dewey, Madison, Medhavy, Musinique, Mycroft, Popper. Week One flagged this. Re measured this week, it has not changed.
beats.new_visual_element: Typeset inventory of the six undecodable project names

beats.narration_text: The audit also found repeats. All Projects appears in two different columns. So does Musinique. Small things individually, but together they tell a visitor the structure was grown rather than designed.

Now typography. The homepage runs nineteen distinct text styles across eight font sizes, in a single family. Weight seven hundred, the bold, is used at six of those eight sizes. The hierarchy problem, stated precisely: many sizes, almost no levels.
beats.new_visual_element: Four stat blocks — 19 styles / 8 sizes / 1 family / bold at 6 of 8

beats.narration_text: The proposal keeps four sizes and gives each one a job. Sixty pixels for display, thirty six for headline, twenty for subhead, sixteen for body, with fourteen reserved for captions and legal text. Bold stops at headline. Below that, weight carries meaning instead of decoration.
beats.new_visual_element: Four-step type scale ladder with the real pixel values, built rung by rung

beats.narration_text: Line length was measured, not guessed. The longest body paragraphs run eighty four characters per line. Comfortable reading sits between forty five and seventy five. The fix is a maximum width on the text column, which costs nothing and buys back read speed.
beats.new_visual_element: Measure bar — 84 characters against the 45-75 comfortable band

beats.narration_text: The accessibility finding is the sharpest of the week. The site's secondary text color is a mid grey that measures four point one two to one against white. W C A G double A requires four point five. Sixty four elements use it, fifty two of them at body size. Darkening that grey by seven levels clears the standard.
beats.new_visual_element: Two swatch rows — #7D7D7D FAIL 4.12:1 against #767676 PASS 4.54:1

beats.narration_text: The accent color was audited the same way. Above the fold there are four maroon buttons, all the same fill, all the same height: Youtube, Donate, About Us, Contact Us. Four equal emphases is the same as none.
beats.new_visual_element: Hero screenshot, red boxes on all four maroon CTAs simultaneously

beats.narration_text: Which brings the hero back. Measured off the same screenshot, the video embed occupies two point one times the area of the entire message column. The value proposition, who this is for and what to do next, holds twenty six percent of the frame.
beats.new_visual_element: Hero screenshot, two measured boxes — media block against message column

beats.narration_text: The direction being explored is a principle, not a layout: order the hero around what a first time visitor expects to find first, rather than around what is easiest to feature. Same content. Different priority.
beats.new_visual_element: Statement card — the hero principle, no layout shown

shot.hold_reason: No proposed hero layout is drawn. Per the presenter: the site's hero is not shown altered, because no redesign has been settled — the beat states the intent only.

beats.narration_text: Week One was the audit. Week Two turned it into a specification: a type scale, a contrast target, a line length, and a hero with its priorities the right way round. Week Three builds it.
beats.new_visual_element: Title card — WEEK 2 WAS THE SPEC

beats.narration_text: Humanitarians dot A I restructure. Week two of four.
